China's first Shenzhou orbital test — opened the path to crewed PRC spaceflight

First flight of the Shenzhou crewed-spacecraft programme. Launched 1999-11-19 22:30 UTC from Jiuquan on the inaugural flight of the human-rated Long March 2F (CZ-2F). The capsule completed 14 orbits at 195 × 315 km, 42.6° inclination, and re-entered to recovery on the Inner Mongolia steppe 1999-11-20 19:41 UTC. Carried a dummy payload and about 100 kg of seeds exposed to the space environment. Marked China's commitment to follow the USSR / USA into independent crewed spaceflight; led, after three more uncrewed tests, to Shenzhou 5 (2003) with Yang Liwei.
Long March 2F maiden flight from Jiuquan LA-4 at 1999-11-19 22:30 UTC.
Capsule descended to Dorbod Banner, Inner Mongolia, 1999-11-20 19:41 UTC.
